merger_description:
Evans Bidco Pty Ltd (**Evans Bidco**), an entity 50% indirectly owned by funds managed by Crescent Capital Partners Management Pty Limited (**Crescent Capital**), 49% indirectly owned by Timothy Vorbach and 1% indirectly owned by Jocelyn Jacomina Rosales and Mateo Tarun Roseles, proposes to acquire Humanverse Pty Ltd, the ultimate holding company of TOA Global Pty Ltd (**TOA Global**) (the **Acquisition**).

Evans Bidco holds 100% of the shares in Emapta Hold Co Pte. Ltd. (**Emapta**). Emapta is a Singapore-registered provider of outsourcing services (including workforce migration, Employer of Record services, and workforce transformation advisory services) to customers across a range of industries, such as finance and accounting, retail, private equity, IT, real estate, logistics, healthcare, and telecommunications and energy.

Crescent Capital is an alternative asset manager covering Australian and New Zealand private equity, private credit and active listed equities.

TOA Global is located on the Gold Coast in Queensland, Australia, and provides outsourced staffing solutions globally, connecting individuals in the Philippines with international companies to meet their staffing requirements. TOA Global operates across Australia, the USA, Canada, Philippines, South Africa, and India.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers
that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening
of competition given:
a. there is small horizontal overlap between Emapta and TOA
Global in the supply of BPO services to Australian
customers, with each of the parties focussed on distinct
service segments
b. the parties’ combined share in the supply of BPO services to
Australian customers from delivery centres in the Philippines
is estimated to be low and the increase in share of supply
arising from the Acquisition is expected to be small
c. there are alternative suppliers of BPO services to Australian
customers that operate in the Philippines, as well as in other
BPO delivery markets including India, Vietnam, and others.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
